data.why: The app is a single self-contained HTML file with no build step; all data comes from live queries to the public iNaturalist API (plus optional OpenStreetMap/Esri), so there is nothing to seed or upload.

goals: Find a place or region and see which parts of it have the fewest iNaturalist observation records
Set a grid size, taxon group, and date range to scope a survey-priority scan
Run a scan and inspect the ranked list of under-sampled grid cells
Click into a specific cell to see its observation count, species list, and observer count before deciding whether to survey it
Export the ranked grid as CSV or GeoJSON for use in GIS or field planning
Compare standard per-cell scanning against the faster tile-based scan mode for larger areas

review.summary: The tree's goal matches what the README says the tool is for: finding the least-recorded cells of a region and planning surveys there. Its phases follow the README's workflow, and most of the screens I opened show what their nodes say. Before filing, it needs a few things: the missing boundary-upload, iNat link-out and why-is-this-cell-empty tasks; the display-housekeeping phase cut; corrected labels for standard mode and the GeoJSON fields; and the screens behind the tile-check and export claims re-cited or dropped.
